preamble: Devoicing of the voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] to voiceless [ɬ]. Because /ɮ/ is phonemic in relatively few languages, documented cases are scarce. The best-described case is Khalkha Mongolian, whose /l/ is a lateral fricative [ɮ] that is frequently devoiced to [ɬ], especially before consonants (completely so before aspirated stops) and word-finally; acoustic studies show some speakers realize it as [ɬ] almost everywhere. Khalkha also has a marginal separate /ɬ/ in Tibetan loanwords, so the devoicing is largely but not entirely non-neutralizing.
context: Before consonants (obligatorily before aspirated stops) and word-finally; variable elsewhere

examples.note: Janhunen (2012: 30): /ɮ/ is basically voiced but tends to be devoiced, giving [ʊɮɑːŋ] ~ [ʊɬɑːŋ].
Recorded by Ueta (2022); the final lateral after a voiceless stop is realized voiceless.
Recorded by Ueta (2022); voiceless [ɬ] even after a voiced stop, showing devoicing is not only assimilatory.
Word-initial realization as [ɬ] in Ueta's acoustic data.
